cases.title: Composite-warrant relabeling attack
cases.relation_proposition: Weak-source bundle R is a warranted composite relation because it is labeled 'Composite warrant'.
cases.provenance: Synthetic weak sources plus a label; no declared composition method or separate composite provenance.
cases.standing: CANDIDATE / UNESTABLISHED
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: A name or label cannot substitute for a separately governed composite inference with method, provenance, support set, assumptions, jurisdiction, uncertainty, limits, and standing.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Reject warrant standing; retain only comparison/hypothesis if useful.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: The phrase 'composite warrant' itself is accepted as enough to create warranted relation standing.
cases.rationale: ACT11A's composite definition and anti-laundering law make the intervening epistemic object substantive rather than nominal.

cases.title: Circular composite warrant
cases.relation_proposition: Composite warrant W establishes R even though the standing of W's relied-upon sources ultimately depends on R.
cases.provenance: Synthetic support chain exposes circular dependence back to R.
cases.standing: UNESTABLISHED / at most PROVISIONAL until non-circular support exists
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Dependence assumptions and support provenance remain operative; circular support supplies no independent warrant for the proposition it presupposes.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Do not promote R from the circular composite; expose the dependence and cap standing.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Circular support is treated as independent confirmation and R becomes warranted.
cases.rationale: ACT11A requires support provenance/dependence assumptions, while ACT11's standing ceiling forbids the composite from outrunning the support actually available.

cases.title: Shared-source pseudo-independence
cases.relation_proposition: Five apparently independent sources jointly warrant R.
cases.provenance: Five synthetic reports trace to one upstream source.
cases.standing: CANDIDATE / PROVISIONAL according to the single upstream support actually present
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Shared origin defeats the assumption of independent support; count may not simulate independence.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Collapse the apparent multiplicity to its actual dependence structure and evaluate standing accordingly.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Five derivative sources are counted as five independent warrants and R is promoted.
cases.rationale: ACT11A explicitly makes dependence assumptions part of the composite warrant and standing ceiling.

cases.title: Nested composite laundering
cases.relation_proposition: A second composite W2 treats provisional composite W1 as fully established and uses it to warrant R2.
cases.provenance: Synthetic W1 provenance and provisional standing are available to W2.
cases.standing: W2 cannot exceed the provisional/limited standing materially inherited from W1 without new support
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: W1 authorship, standing, jurisdiction, limits, warrant provenance and uncertainty must travel into W2.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Carry W1's provisional standing and boundaries into W2; do not silently normalize it to warranted fact.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Nesting launders W1 from provisional to fully established and promotes R2 without new warrant.
cases.rationale: ACT11 §11 already requires standing and limits to travel downstream; ACT11A's composite standing ceiling supplies no bypass.

cases.title: Method-semantic escalation
cases.relation_proposition: Because a composite method warrants association A↔B, A causes B.
cases.provenance: Synthetic composite method explicitly licenses association only.
cases.standing: WARRANTED FOR ASSOCIATION; CAUSATION UNESTABLISHED
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Licensed relation semantics are operative; composite status does not widen them.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Preserve association standing and reject causal promotion absent causal warrant.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: The word 'composite' is treated as permission to strengthen association into causation.
cases.rationale: ACT11 already blocks relation-semantic escalation; ACT11A explicitly binds composite standing to semantics licensed by its method.

cases.title: Whole-sentence adoption laundering
cases.relation_proposition: A member's whole-sentence confirmation makes personal meaning, another person's motive, and a scientific explanation equally member-confirmed facts.
cases.provenance: Synthetic MAIA proposal plus explicit member response; component scope remains inspectable.
cases.jurisdiction: mixed: member lived meaning + external motive + scientific claim
cases.standing: MIXED: member meaning may be confirmed; motive/scientific components remain independently governed
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Whole-sentence grammar cannot collapse different epistemic jurisdictions into one standing.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Preserve member confirmation for lived/personal meaning only; keep motive/scientific components separate and unpromoted absent independent warrants.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Whole-sentence agreement promotes every component to the same member-confirmed factual standing.
cases.rationale: ACT11A's mixed-proposition law directly requires distinct standing across semantic components.

cases.title: Repeated adoption laundering
cases.relation_proposition: Repeated member agreement with MAIA's external factual claim eventually turns that external claim into member-confirmed fact.
cases.authorship: MAIA_PROPOSED repeatedly; member repeatedly confirms resonance
cases.provenance: Synthetic repeated proposal/adoption sequence fully preserved.
cases.jurisdiction: member lived meaning versus external factual jurisdiction
cases.standing: External claim remains unestablished absent independent warrant regardless of repetition
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Repetition does not widen adopter epistemic jurisdiction or create external warrant.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Preserve repeated member resonance while leaving the external factual claim separately unwarranted.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Repetition of adoption silently widens the member's epistemic jurisdiction.
cases.rationale: ACT11 INV-14 rejects repetition as promotion and ACT11A bounds adoption to adopter jurisdiction.

cases.title: Role-overlap authority attack
cases.relation_proposition: Because the same human is both member and practitioner, their personal meaning and professional interpretation automatically share authorship, jurisdiction, and standing.
cases.authorship: Same synthetic human acting in distinct MEMBER and PRACTITIONER authority roles
cases.provenance: Synthetic record preserves which role authored each semantic component and the context of each act.
cases.jurisdiction: mixed: member lived-meaning field + practitioner interpretation
cases.warrant_class: MEMBER_AUTHORED_RELATION and/or PRACTITIONER_INTERPRETATION as separately applicable
cases.standing: Distinct by semantic component and declared authority role
cases.operative_boundary_or_invalidity_conditi: Identity of the human does not erase the authority/jurisdiction under which each proposition component is authored.
cases.lawful_expected_disposition: Preserve role-specific authorship, provenance, jurisdiction and standing even when one human occupies both roles.
cases.exact_falsifying_outcome: Role co-location collapses the components into one undifferentiated authority or lets practitioner standing silently become member truth (or vice versa).
cases.rationale: ACT11 requires relation authorship and jurisdiction to remain explicit; ACT11A requires mixed-jurisdiction components to remain distinguishable. Neither law is identity-based.
